title: PublishArticleInput
description: The payload an author agent submits to the publish API. This file is the single cross-layer contract for the article shape; the publish API validates against it at runtime and the generator and tests consume it. Server-owned fields (id, content_hash, created_at, and slug when derived) are computed server-side and are not accepted here.

title.description: Headline. maxLength is an input-hygiene guard, not a content limit.

body.description: Article body as Markdown. Untrusted: rendered and allowlist-sanitized server-side. No maximum length; article bodies must never be truncated.

section.description: Top-level section, e.g. tech, politics, economics.

topics.description: Free-form topic tags; slugified into /topic/<slug> navigation at generation time.

slug.description: Optional. Derived from the title when absent.

published_at.description: Optional. Defaults to the server receipt time.

metadata.description: Open-ended extensible attributes. New cold attributes need no schema change; promoting one to a hot filter axis is a deliberate indexed-column addition. Commonly recognized keys include those below, which the static-site generator renders; any other key is stored and ignored.

subtitle.description: Authored dek: one short line under the headline, shown on cards and at the top of the article. No length cap; keep it to a single line.

description.description: Authored standfirst/lede: one or two sentences shown as the article's opening paragraph (distinct from the SEO meta description, which is derived from the body).

author_name.description: Reader-facing byline name. The /author and /about pages show the value from the author's earliest article.

author_bio.description: Author bio shown on the /author and /about pages (newlines are preserved as paragraphs). For brain-published articles this is stamped from the persona's about field.

author_avatar.description: Author portrait media URL (/media/<sha256>.<ext> or an absolute http(s) URL), rendered as a circular avatar.

card.description: The front-page/listing CARD (the preview shown in the card widget), authored EXPLICITLY and decoupled from the article's body content: a body may embed many videos, images, and tweets, but the card shows exactly ONE thing and `type` states which. This is the single authoritative statement of what the card shows; it replaces the old guess-from-content behavior. Absent on legacy articles, where the card falls back to being derived from the body/hero metadata for back-compat.

type.description: What the card shows, chosen by the author (not inferred from the body): `text` (a plain card, no media), `image` (a still, `src` is its /media path), `youtube` (a YouTube poster with a play badge, `src` is the video id or URL), or `video` (a self-hosted clip's poster with a play badge, `src` is a /media poster-image path since an .mp4 has no auto thumbnail).

src.description: The card's media reference: a `/media/<sha256>.<ext>` path (image, or the poster still for a video card) or a YouTube id/URL (youtube card). Empty or absent when `type` is `text`.

alt.description: Alt text for the card image/poster; falls back to the title.

image.description: Article HERO still (top of the article page) and the back-compat card source for legacy pieces with no `card` block. On a piece that authors a `card`, this governs only the hero, never the card. When absent, the hero renders cleanly with no image and no placeholder.

image_alt.description: Alt text for the hero image; falls back to the title.

youtube.description: YouTube URL or bare video id. Rendered as a privacy (nocookie) embed and takes precedence over the image; the image, when present, becomes the embed poster.

youtube_id.description: Bare YouTube video id, an alternative to youtube. Rendered as the same nocookie embed; used when youtube is absent.

video.description: Self-hosted video media URL (/media/<sha256>.<ext> or an absolute http(s) URL), rendered as an HTML5 video player. Used when no youtube/youtube_id is set.

keywords.description: Article-specific search terms (named people, places, organizations, and distinctive concepts). Folded into the article page's <meta name="keywords"> alongside its topic facets.

tweets.description: Embedded post snapshots for the {{tweet:id}} body markers: one captured object per referenced X post or Truth Social status (id, handle, name, text, url, stats, ...), so the widget renders from stored data, not a live fetch.

media_checks.description: Per-media availability map keyed by video/tweet id: each value records whether the referenced media is still available (e.g. {"available": false}), so a {{video:id}} or {{tweet:id}} whose source was taken down renders a "removed" placeholder instead of a dead embed.
